Metzudat David: R. David Altschuler and his son Yechiel, Prague and Galicia, 18th century
Metzudat Zion: R. David Altschuler and his son Yechiel, Prague and Galicia, 18th century
Malbim: R. Meir Leibush Wisser, Eastern Europe, 1809–1879
Abarbanel: Don Isaac Abarbanel, Lisbon, Naples and Venice, 1437–1508
Ibn Ezra: Abraham ibn Ezra, Spain, Italy and France, 1089–1167
Targum Jonathan: the Aramaic translation of the Prophets, Land of Israel and Babylonia, 1st–4th centuries CE
Jerusalem Talmud: the Talmud of the Land of Israel, Tiberias and Caesarea, c. 400 CE
Mishnah: the Mishnah, Land of Israel, c. 200 CE
Tosefta: a companion collection to the Mishnah, Land of Israel, 3rd century CE
Midrash: rabbinic midrash, Land of Israel, 3rd–10th centuries CE
Bereshit Rabbah: midrash on Genesis, Land of Israel, 5th century CE
Midrash Rabbah: the classic midrash collections on the Torah and the Five Scrolls, Land of Israel, 5th–12th centuries CE
Kohelet Rabbah: midrash on Ecclesiastes, Land of Israel, c. 8th century CE
Tanchuma: homiletic midrash on the Torah, Land of Israel, 5th–9th centuries CE
Midrash Tehillim: midrash on Psalms (Shocher Tov), compiled over centuries, completed in the Middle Ages
Yalkut Shimoni: an anthology of midrash on the whole Bible, attributed to R. Shimon ha-Darshan, Germany, 13th century
Ein Yaakov: the Talmud's stories and teachings, gathered by R. Jacob ibn Habib, Salonika, early 16th century
Mekhilta: halakhic midrash on Exodus, Land of Israel, 3rd century CE
Sifre: halakhic midrash on Numbers and Deuteronomy, Land of Israel, 3rd century CE
Pesikta: homiletic midrash, Land of Israel, 5th–7th centuries CE
Pesikta Rabbati: homiletic midrash for the festivals and special Shabbatot, Land of Israel, 6th–9th centuries CE
Pirkei Avot: the Mishnah's tractate of sayings, c. 200 CE
Zohar: the classic work of Kabbalah, attributed to R. Shimon bar Yochai, Castile, late 13th century
Lekha Dodi: the Friday-night hymn of R. Shlomo Alkabetz, Safed, 16th century
Abudarham: R. David Abudarham, commentary on the prayers, Seville, 14th century
Minchat Shai: R. Yedidiah Shlomo Norzi, notes on the Masoretic text, Mantua, c. 1560–1626
Tze'enah Ure'enah: R. Jacob ben Isaac Ashkenazi of Janów, Yiddish retelling of the Torah and haftarot, Poland, c. 1600
Chomat Anakh: R. Chaim Yosef David Azulai (the Chida), Jerusalem and Livorno, 1724–1806
Shadal: Samuel David Luzzatto, Trieste and Padua, 1800–1865
Fox: Everett Fox, translator of the Hebrew Bible, b. 1947
